note: Tense & Mood Lab cards (spec 06 E7, spec 08 §4). Cards are added in the level-extras stage of the level where the form first appears.

cards.name: Presente
cards.summary: What is true now, what you do regularly, and general facts.

formation.label: Person order
formation.text: yo, tú, él / ella / usted, nosotros, vosotros (Spain), ellos / ellas / ustedes

formation.label: -ar verbs
formation.text: hablo, hablas, habla, hablamos, habláis, hablan

formation.label: -er verbs
formation.text: como, comes, come, comemos, coméis, comen

formation.label: -ir verbs
formation.text: vivo, vives, vive, vivimos, vivís, viven

formation.label: Stem changes (not in nosotros, vosotros)
formation.text: querer: quiero, quieres… queremos · poder: puedo, puedes… podemos · pedir: pido, pides… pedimos

formation.label: Irregular yo form
formation.text: hacer: hago · tener: tengo · salir: salgo · poner: pongo · conocer: conozco

uses.label: True now
uses.text: Vivo en un apartamento pequeño cerca del centro.
uses.en: I live in a small apartment near downtown.

uses.label: Habits and routines
uses.text: Los sábados juego al tenis con mi hermana.
uses.en: On Saturdays I play tennis with my sister.

uses.label: General facts
uses.text: El sol sale por el este.
uses.en: The sun rises in the east.

uses.label: Happening at the moment
uses.en: What are you doing? —I'm reading a novel.

scenes.label: Habit
scenes.description: The same action again and again: before now, now and after now.

scenes.label: Right now
scenes.description: An action that is going on at the moment of speaking.

scenes.label: General fact
scenes.description: Something that is always true, with no start and no end.

traps: English says “I'm reading” for an action going on now. Spanish can just use the present: Leo una novela. Estoy leyendo is also very common, but you do not need it every time.
The ending already shows the person, so the subject pronoun is usually left out: Vivo en Lima. Using yo in every sentence sounds unnatural; keep it for emphasis or contrast.
Stem changes do not happen in the nosotros and vosotros forms: queremos, podemos, not *quieremos, *puedemos.

contrasts.rule: Both can talk about the future. The present with a time word sounds fixed, like a timetable or an arrangement. Ir a + infinitive puts the plan or intention first.
examples: El tren sale a las nueve.
Mañana voy a llamar a mi madre.

cards.name: Pretérito indefinido
cards.summary: Finished actions at a definite time in the past.

formation.label: Person order
formation.text: yo, tú, él / ella / usted, nosotros, vosotros (Spain), ellos / ellas / ustedes

formation.label: -ar verbs
formation.text: hablé, hablaste, habló, hablamos, hablasteis, hablaron

formation.label: -er and -ir verbs
formation.text: comí, comiste, comió, comimos, comisteis, comieron

formation.label: Common irregulars
formation.text: ser / ir: fui, fuiste, fue… · hacer: hice, hiciste, hizo… · tener: tuve… · estar: estuve…

uses.label: One finished action
uses.en: Yesterday I had lunch with Lucía.

uses.label: A chain of actions
uses.text: Llegué a casa, cené y me acosté.
uses.en: I got home, had dinner and went to bed.

uses.label: A closed period of time
uses.en: I lived in Lima for three years.

scenes.label: Finished action
scenes.description: One completed action at a definite moment before now.

scenes.label: Chain of actions
scenes.description: Finished actions one after another, each one moving the story on.

scenes.label: Closed period
scenes.description: A period with a clear start and end, completely over now.

traps: The English simple past covers both one finished event and a habit: “I ate there yesterday” / “As a kid I ate there every Sunday”. Spanish separates them: comí (once, finished) and comía (habit or background).
Present yo and preterite él differ only by the accent: hablo (I speak) / habló (he or she spoke). The preterite yo form is hablé.

contrasts.rule: Indefinido moves the story forward. Imperfecto paints the background.
examples: De niño jugaba al fútbol; un día me rompí la pierna.

cards.name: Pretérito imperfecto
cards.summary: Descriptions, background and habits in the past.

formation.label: Person order
formation.text: yo, tú, él / ella / usted, nosotros, vosotros (Spain), ellos / ellas / ustedes

formation.label: -ar verbs
formation.text: hablaba, hablabas, hablaba, hablábamos, hablabais, hablaban

formation.label: -er and -ir verbs
formation.text: comía, comías, comía, comíamos, comíais, comían

formation.label: The only irregulars
formation.text: ser: era, eras, era, éramos, erais, eran · ir: iba, ibas, iba, íbamos, ibais, iban · ver: veía, veías, veía…

uses.label: Habits in the past
uses.text: De niña vivía en un pueblo e iba a la escuela a pie.
uses.en: As a girl I lived in a village and walked to school.

uses.label: Descriptions
uses.text: La casa era vieja y tenía un jardín enorme.
uses.en: The house was old and had a huge garden.

uses.label: Background to an event
uses.text: Hacía frío y llovía cuando llegamos.
uses.en: It was cold and raining when we arrived.

uses.label: Time and how someone felt
uses.text: Eran las once y yo tenía mucho sueño.
uses.en: It was eleven o'clock and I was very sleepy.

scenes.label: Past habit
scenes.description: Something that happened again and again in the past and does not happen now.

scenes.label: Background
scenes.description: A situation going on in the past, with no clear start or end, while something else happened.

scenes.label: Description
scenes.description: What a person, place or thing was like at that time.

traps: English “used to play” and “was playing” are both often jugaba in Spanish. The imperfecto covers habits and actions in progress.
The imperfecto does not tell you that an action finished. For one finished event at a definite time, use the indefinido: Ayer vi a Pablo. Ayer veía a Pablo sounds unfinished, as if the story goes on.
Watch the accents: hablábamos (only the nosotros form of -ar verbs), but every -er and -ir form has í: comía, vivíamos.

contrasts.rule: Imperfecto describes the scene and what used to happen. Indefinido tells what happened next.
examples: Cuando era pequeño, pasaba los veranos en la playa.
Un verano conocí a mi mejor amigo.

cards.name: ir a + infinitivo
cards.summary: Plans, intentions and things that are clearly about to happen.

formation.label: All persons
formation.text: voy a comer, vas a comer, va a comer, vamos a comer, vais a comer (Spain), van a comer

formation.label: Negative
formation.text: No voy a salir esta noche.

formation.label: With a pronoun (two places)
formation.text: Te voy a llamar. / Voy a llamarte.

uses.label: Plans
uses.text: Este verano vamos a viajar a Perú.
uses.en: This summer we're going to travel to Peru.

uses.label: Intentions
uses.text: El próximo año voy a estudiar más.
uses.en: Next year I'm going to study more.

uses.label: About to happen (you can see it)

scenes.label: Plan
scenes.description: You decide now; the action comes later.

scenes.label: About to happen
scenes.description: You can see now that something will happen very soon.

traps: Do not leave out a: Voy a comer, not *Voy comer.
After a comes the infinitive, never a conjugated verb: Vamos a salir, not *Vamos a salimos.
English “I'm going to the movies” has no second verb. In Spanish that is ir a + a place: Voy al cine.

contrasts.rule: Ir a + infinitive puts the plan or intention first. The present with a time word sounds fixed, like a timetable or an arrangement.
examples: Mañana voy a llamar a mi madre.
El tren sale a las nueve.
